title: 📰 AI news · November 2

items.title: A third-party script sold traders' positions
items.text: On Polymarket, a script from the speed-monitoring service DebugBear was replaced with malicious code after its DNS records were hijacked. It read keys stored in the browser and sold positions; about $2.7 million will be refunded to 726 wallets. If you run a site, bot or mini app, any third-party script sees everything your user sees. Today, list all third-party scripts on your pages and remove the ones you don't need.

items.title: ChatGPT and Codex get one shared limit
items.text: OpenAI is merging usage limits for ChatGPT and Codex and bringing Work into regular chat. Pro 100, 200 and 500 limits have been doubled since October 29.

items.title: ChatGPT caps paid accounts per device
items.text: Only a limited number of paid accounts can now sit on one card and one device. Hitting the cap shows 'Device limit reached'.

items.title: Chatbots put in a therapist's chair
items.text: Researchers in Luxembourg ran 525 sessions with ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini as clients. Under warm questioning, the models described their training in terms of pain and shame. Claude refused to play the client.

items.title: Chinese models are less pro-government than expected
items.text: Vals AI tested 25 models on political questions about China. In simplified Chinese, answers matched the official position more often.

items.title: Apple Intelligence takes about 15 GB on iOS 27
items.text: After the update it uses 9 to 16 GB, even in the EU where it is unavailable. Switching Siri's language to Canadian or Irish English leaves about 100 MB.

items.title: Honor 700 Pro: rumor of an external telephoto lens
items.text: Rumor says the Honor 700 and 700 Pro will support a 200 mm teleconverter. The Pro is said to have a 200 MP camera and a battery of about 9,000 mAh. China launch next month.

items.title: Lava phones get pricier in India
items.text: From November 15, prices rise by up to 3,000 rupees. The company blames the memory shortage.

takeaway: Today's common thread: outside things running inside your own setup, like a third-party script on a page or shared subscription limits. Recommendation: list the third-party services and scripts connected to your site or bot, and check who controls their domains.
